title: SYSK Selects: How Homelessness Works
summary: Saturday Selects rerun of the 2010 Stuff You Should Know episode on homelessness in the United States. Chuck introduces it as a fan favorite that drew criticism from listeners who felt homeless people deserve their situation. The hosts discuss homeless counts (point-in-time counts and Census Bureau annual estimates), rising homeless school children numbers, the link between poverty, minimum wage, and lack of affordable housing, the demolition of public housing like Techwood in Atlanta, mental illness (including the Reagan-era deinstitutionalization claim), addiction, domestic violence, veterans, health effects of homelessness, the McKinney-Vento Act, Section 8 housing, food banks and food waste, ways to help, and the invisibility of homeless people. The episode closes with a Kiva listener mail round-up and a holiday story call.

segments.title: Selects intro and Facebook banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces the Selects episode, explaining it is the homelessness episode from 2010 that drew listener criticism. The hosts banter about Facebook posts and Bonnie Prince Billy.

segments.title: Homeless school children and counting the homeless
segments.summary: Josh cites a July report of rising homeless school children, with state-level increases such as Texas and Iowa. The hosts explain point-in-time counts and annual Census Bureau estimates, and note the difficulty of counting people in cars or campgrounds.

segments.title: Homelessness around the world and in the US
segments.summary: The hosts give worldwide estimates from the UN and compare Sweden and Norway with the US. They note racial disproportion, with African Americans making up a large share of the homeless population, and that homeless families are proportionally common in rural areas. They also discuss the broad definition of homelessness.

segments.title: Poverty, minimum wage, and affordable housing
segments.summary: The hosts identify poverty and the lack of affordable housing as major drivers. They explain the poverty line, how federal minimum wage income falls below it, and that affording a two-bedroom apartment at minimum wage would require very long weeks. Many homeless people have jobs, and people can fall into homelessness after job loss or medical bills.

segments.title: Demolition of public housing and Techwood
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the demolition of Techwood housing in Atlanta before the Olympics and a nationwide trend from 1980 to 2003 in which more than two million low-rent units were demolished or converted, while federal housing assistance was cut by half.

segments.title: Mental illness, Reagan, and addiction
segments.summary: About twenty percent of homeless people have a mental illness. The hosts discuss the claim that Reagan's closing of state psychiatric hospitals and funding cuts contributed to homelessness. They also note that about two-thirds of homeless people struggle with alcohol or drug problems.

segments.title: McKinney-Vento Act and domestic violence
segments.summary: Reagan signed the McKinney-Vento Act, which funded shelters, transitional housing, healthcare, food, and job training. The hosts describe domestic violence as a major factor, especially for women and runaway kids, and note that homeless people face further abuse on the street.

segments.title: Veterans and effects of homelessness
segments.summary: Veterans make up a significant share of homeless people, often with PTSD or substance abuse. The hosts then discuss physical attacks on homeless people and health effects for adults and children, including stomach problems, asthma, depression, PTSD, frostbite, and HIV.

segments.title: Shelters, Section 8, food banks, and job training
segments.summary: The hosts describe homeless shelters, Section 8 vouchers with long waiting lists, and public housing. They discuss food banks, food waste estimates of up to half of food produced, and job training programs such as First Step and the Homeless Veterans Reintegration Program.

segments.title: How to help and seeing homeless people as people
segments.summary: The hosts list ways to help: volunteering, donating goods or cars, advocacy, and hiring homeless people. They discuss the invisibility of homeless people, mention Will Smith's story, and cite a photography book and a photo project that give homeless people names and identities.

segments.title: Kiva round-up and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts explain Kiva microlending and report on the show's Kiva team. They read listener mail from a teen jewelry-making fan who sells items to fund Kiva loans, and a plug for an Army Kiva team. They close with a call for holiday stories.
